title: Temporal Signal Horizon Swap Controller with Decay-based Rollback
author: Arjun Patel
description:
Context and motivation: Our current rollout controllers focus on instantaneous metrics (latency/err-rate) and cohort partitioning. That makes short-lived signal spikes (traffic bursts, transient infra flakiness) cause noisy rollbacks or overly conservative holds. This PR introduces a Temporal Signal Horizon Swap Controller: a rollout orchestration component that smooths short-lived metric spikes across a configurable decay horizon and gates model swaps by a time-weighted anomaly budget. The goal is to reduce noisy rollbacks while preserving quick safety responses for sustained degradations.

What this PR changes (high level):
- New controller: pkg/rollouts/temporal_horizon_controller.go implementing the horizon window and decay weighting.
- Decay policy library: pkg/rollouts/decay_policy.go + tests, exposes configurable half-life and weighting functions.
- Swap executor updates: services/orchestrator/swap_executor.go updated to consult horizon controller decisions and produce safe swap transactions with checkpointed rollback markers.
- Safety journal: deployments/rollback_journal/entry.go — lightweight append-only log for post-mortem playback and deterministic rollback.
- E2E tests: deployments/e2e/temporal_horizon_swap_test.go (simulates transient spikes vs sustained regressions).
- Docs: docs/runbooks/temporal-signal-swap.md and examples/rollouts/temporal_horizon.yaml.

Key design points:
- Time-weighting: recent observations are decayed with an exponential half-life so a single short spike contributes less to the aggregate anomaly score than sustained regressions.
- Two-stage gating: the controller exposes a fast-fail gate (immediate severe-signal abort) and a smoothed gate (time-weighted score must exceed threshold for t_window).
- Safety budget: rollouts are allocated a small anomaly budget per cohort. If the budget is exhausted, the controller triggers an automated rollback and escalates telemetry.
- Deterministic rollback markers: swap_executor writes a checkpoint to the rollback journal before switching traffic. Rollback replays are deterministic and recorded for audits.

Operational notes / runbook excerpt:
- Default half-life: 60s. To accelerate sensitivity set half_life_seconds to 20; to be more conservative set to 180.
- If rollout.budget_remaining hits 0, controller triggers automated rollback and creates an incident with SUP-4321 template.
- To debug a rollback: use deployments/rollback_journal replay with --trace flag to produce deterministic request-level replay.

Why this is different: Instead of only partitioning users/cohorts, the controller reasons over time and signal persistence: short spikes are de-emphasized, sustained problems trigger rapid rollback. This reduces noisy user-facing rollbacks and improves rollout stability across bursty workloads.
